title: Sum a variable number of arguments
description: Write a function `sum_all(*args)` that accepts any number of positional numeric arguments and returns their sum. Calling it with no arguments should return 0.
hints: The function needs to accept any number of arguments, not just a fixed count.
Prefixing a parameter with `*`, like `*args`, collects all positional arguments into a tuple inside the function.
Since `args` is just a tuple of numbers, you can pass it directly to the built-in `sum()` function and return the result.
expected_behavior: Returns the sum of all positional arguments passed in; returns 0 if no arguments are passed.
explanation: The `*args` syntax gathers every positional argument the function is called with into a single tuple named `args`. `sum()` then adds up all the numbers in that tuple, naturally returning 0 when the tuple is empty.
